category_match: The shell follows the Intercom workspace pattern, but the Home content still reads as a generic dashboard rather than a focused operational workspace.
differences: Setup is presented as a small sidebar utility instead of the dominant, structured first-run workspace shown in the reference.
The four operational totals have limited numeric hierarchy and blend into a flat strip.
Downloading, searches, missing media and events are separated into similarly weighted blocks, which weakens scan order.
Health and system facts are useful real data, but their relationship to setup readiness and daily operations is not visually explicit.
The content density is lower and the section rhythm less deliberate than the compact Intercom reference surface.
suggestions: Promote incomplete setup into a wide onboarding workspace with progress, one clear next action and compact remaining-step rows.
Use a measured metric band with larger values, restrained labels and shared dividers.
Group live operational feeds into a denser activity workspace with stronger headings and row-level dividers.
Use real health, source, downloader and library-folder facts as the supporting readiness panel instead of decorative imagery.
Keep mobile layouts stacked with 44px minimum interactive targets rather than shrinking the desktop composition.
reasoning: The existing page already exposes the right live information and actions. The needed change is hierarchy: setup should guide new installations, metrics should establish status at a glance, and daily activity should read as one coherent work area. The adaptation should use only current HolyArrs data and routes.
